title: Second French Empire
capsule: The Second French Empire was the regime of Emperor Napoleon III (Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte), who came to power via a coup d'état on 2 December 1851 and was proclaimed emperor exactly one year later, replacing the Second Republic. The regime's first decade was characterised by authoritarian rule, rapid industrialisation, Baron Haussmann's transformation of Paris, and foreign adventurism—including French victory in the Crimean War (1853–56), intervention in Italy aiding Piedmont against Austria in 1859, and the disastrous Mexican intervention (1861–67). Napoleon III's declaration of war on Prussia in July 1870 ended in catastrophe: defeated at Sedan on 2 September 1870 and captured, he abdicated, and the Third Republic was proclaimed in Paris on 4 September 1870; the formal armistice came in January 1871.
